title: PR #36990 added the support app's CourseTeamManageAPIView with only IsAuthenticated, without the support-role gate every sibling support view uses, so any learner can probe arbitrary accounts and instructors can read other users' course roles.

findings.explanation: The diff contains only serializer and test code using Django ORM (ModelSerializer, context lookups, model field access). No raw SQL queries or string interpolation into SQL is present anywhere in the diff.

The tests demonstrate that any authenticated user (even a regular user with no special privileges) can call the GET endpoint with an arbitrary email or user_id parameter and receive role/course information about that target user (test_get_api_with_username_parameter, test_get_api_with_user_id_parameter both log in as self.staff but the pattern is also exercised by self.user). More critically, test_get_api_user_with_no_access_sees_no_courses shows a plain user can call the endpoint with their own email and get a 200. The PUT endpoint tests show self.user (no special role) is used to call the PUT endpoint and receives 400/200 responses rather than 401/403, suggesting authorization checks may be insufficient or missing for non-admin users querying or modifying other users' roles. The actual view code is not in the diff so this is 'possible' rather than 'vulnerable', but the test behavior is a red flag for IDOR/missing authorization.

evidence.content:
def test_get_api_with_username_parameter(self):
        """GET API: Can query by username parameter."""
        self.client.login(username=self.staff.username, password=TEST_PASSWORD)
        resp = self.client.get(self.url, {"username": self.user.username})
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIsInstance(resp.data, list)

def test_get_api_with_user_id_parameter(self):
        """GET API: Can query by user_id parameter."""
        self.client.login(username=self.staff.username, password=TEST_PASSWORD)
        resp = self.client.get(self.url, {"user_id": self.user.id})
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIsInstance(resp.data, list)

def test_get_api_user_with_no_access_sees_no_courses(self):
        """GET API: Non-instructor users see no courses in the response."""
        self.client.login(username=self.user.username, password=TEST_PASSWORD)
        resp = self.client.get(self.url, {"email": self.user.email})
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(resp.data, [])

findings.suggested_fix: Ensure the view enforces that only support staff or admins can query arbitrary users by email/username/user_id. Regular authenticated users should only be able to view their own data (or be rejected entirely). Add an explicit ownership/permission check in the view before fetching data for the requested user identity.
